farraa:2-2.t: His saying: Alif Lām Mīm ﴿أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوۤاْ﴾: [before] ﴿يُتركوا﴾ the lām of the genitive [li-] can fall; when you remove it from it, it is accusative. They seldom say "I left you that you go (an tadhhaba)"; they only say "I left you going (tadhhabu)". But it has been made self-sufficient by falling upon "the people" alone. And if you make ﴿حَسب﴾ repeated over it, that is correct, as though the meaning were: ﴿أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوۤاْ﴾ — did they think ﴿أَن يَقُولُوۤاْ آمَنَّا وَهُمْ لاَ يُفْتَنُونَ﴾?

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱتَّبِعُواْ سَبِيلَنَا وَلْنَحْمِلْ﴾: it is a command carrying the interpretation of a conditional, just as His saying ﴿ادْخُلُوا مَسَاكِنَكُمْ لاَ يَحْطِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ is a prohibition carrying the interpretation of a conditional. This is frequent in the speech of the Arabs.
The poet said:
فقلتُ ادعِى وأَدْعُ فإنَّ أندى * لصَوتٍ أن يُنَادىَ داعيانِ
(I said: call out, and let me call out, for the farthest-reaching of voices is when two callers call.)
He meant: "call out, and let me call (wa-li-adʿu), for the farthest-reaching…" It is as though he said: if you call, I will call.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَيَحْمِلُنَّ أَثْقَالَهُمْ﴾ means their burdens of sin [142/a] ﴿وَأَثْقَالاً مَّعَ أَثْقَالِهِمْ﴾: he says: the sins of those they led astray.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَاناً وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾: (إنَّما) in this position is a single particle, not in the sense of (الذى) (that which). ﴿وَتَخْلُقُونَ إِفْكاً﴾ is referred back to (إنّما), as in your saying: "You only do such-and-such, and you only do such-and-such." They agree on the light form of ﴿تَخْلُقُونَ﴾, except Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who read (وتَخَلّقُون إفْكا), with fatḥa on the tāʾ and a doubled lām; the two are the same in meaning.

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿ٱلنَّشْأَةَ﴾: the readers agree on a vowelless shīn and a short form, except al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, who lengthened it throughout the Quran and said (النشَاءَة). Similar to it, among what the Arabs say, are al-raʾfa and al-raʾāfa, al-kaʾba and al-kaʾāba; all are correct.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَنتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَلاَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾: Someone may say: how did He describe them as not able to escape (lā yuʿjizūn) on earth or in heaven, when they are not of the people of heaven? The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: you cannot escape on earth, nor can whoever is in heaven escape. This is among the subtleties of Arabic, because of the pronoun [i.e. the omitted relative] that does not appear in the second [part].
Similar is the saying of Ḥassān:
أمَن يهجو رسولَ الله منكم * ويمدحُهُ وينصرهُ سَوَاءٌ
(Is the one of you who satirises the Messenger of Allah, and the one who praises him and helps him, alike?)
He meant: "and whoever helps him and praises him", implying (مَنْ). It may occur to the listener's mind that the praising and helping belong to this overt man [i.e. the satirist]. Similar in ordinary speech: "Honour whoever came to you and came to your father", and "Honour whoever came to you and did not come to Zayd", meaning: and whoever did not come to Zayd.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ إِنَّمَا ٱتَّخَذْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَاناً مَّوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾: Ḥamza read it in the accusative and in a genitive construct; ʿĀṣim and the people of Medina read it in the accusative with tanwīn: ﴿أَوْثَاناً مَّوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾ [Translator's note: the vowelling as printed here shows the construct; the tanwīn reading is mawaddatan baynakum]. Some people, among them al-Kisāʾī, read it in the nominative with the construct. Al-Ḥasan read (مَوَدّةٌ بَيْنَكُمْ), in the nominative without the construct. In the reading of Ubayy: (إنَّما مَوَدَّةُ بَيْنهِمْ فى الحياة الدُّنْيَا), and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (إنَّما مَوَدَّةُ بَيْنِكم); these two are witnesses for whoever reads the nominative. Whoever reads the nominative makes it nominative only by the qualifier (ṣifa, here the prepositional phrase) in His saying ﴿فِي ٱلْحَيَاةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾, and the sentence breaks off at His saying ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱتَّخَذْتُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْثَاناً﴾; then He said: your love of those idols and your worship of them are nothing; it is only an affection among you in the life of this world, and then it ceases. Whoever reads the accusative makes "taking" fall upon it: you have only taken them as [a bond of] affection among you in the life of this world. It may also be nominative by making it the predicate of mā, taking (ما) in the sense of (الذى), as though you said: "Those whom you have taken as idols are [a bond of] affection among you"; then "affection" is like the predicate. Its nominative may also be by an implied (هىَ) (it is), as in His saying ﴿لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلاَّ سَاعةً مِنْ نَهَارٍ﴾, then He said ﴿بَلاَغٌ﴾, i.e. this is a proclamation, that is a proclamation. Similar is ﴿إنَّ الذينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللهِ الكَذِبَ لا يُفْلِحُونَ﴾, then He said ﴿مَتَاعٌ فِى الدنيا﴾, i.e. that is enjoyment in the life of this world. His saying ﴿يَكْفُرُ بَعْضُكُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾: some of you will disown others, and the worshipper and the worshipped will be in the Fire.

farraa:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّي مُهَاجِرٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّيۤ﴾: these are the words of Ibrāhīm. His emigration was from Ḥarrān to Palestine.

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَجْرَهُ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: good praise, and that the people of all religions take him as their patron. And part of his reward is that prophethood and the Book were placed among his descendants.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿وَتَقْطَعُونَ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾: their cutting it was that they used to waylay people on the roads with their foul practice, meaning sodomy. It is also said: "you cut off the way" means you cut off the way of offspring by your neglect of / [142/a] women. His saying ﴿وَتَأْتُونَ فِي نَادِيكُمُ ٱلْمُنْكَرَ﴾: in your gatherings. Among the abominations were flicking pebbles, whistling, chewing gum, undoing the buttons of cloaks and shirts, and shooting with pellets. It is said they were eighteen practices, according to al-Kalbī, which I do not remember. Someone else said: they were ten.

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانُواْ مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ﴾: in their religion. He says: possessed of insight.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمَثَلِ ٱلْعَنكَبُوتِ ٱتَّخَذَتْ بَيْتاً﴾: He struck it as a parable for whoever takes a protector besides Allah: it neither benefits him nor harms him, just as the spider's house does not protect it from heat or cold. The spider is feminine, though some of the Arabs make it masculine. The poet said:
على هَطّالهم منهم بيوتٌ * كأنَّ العنكبوت هو ابتناهَا
(On their mountain Haṭṭāl they have houses, as if the spider — he — had built them.)

farraa:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلصَّلاَةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ وَلَذِكْرُ ٱللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ﴾: he says: Allah's remembering you with reward is better than your remembering Him when you have desisted. It may also be: prayer forbids indecency and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater and more worthy to forbid.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿فَٱلَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ ٱلْكِتَابَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾: in Muhammad ﷺ. It is said that this is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām. ﴿وَمِنْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِهِ﴾ means those of the people of Mecca who believed.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كُنتَ تَتْلُواْ مِن قَبْلِهِ﴾: before the Quran ﴿مِن كِتَابٍ وَلاَ تَخُطُّهُ بِيَمِينِكَ﴾; had you been like that ﴿لاَّرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾ — he means the Christians who found his description. And ﴿لاَّرْتَابَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ﴾ may mean: it would have increased the doubt of those who denied, among the people of Mecca and others.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ هُوَ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ﴾: he means the Quran. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: (بل هى آياتٌ), meaning: rather the verses of the Quran are clear verses. Similar is ﴿هَذَا بَصَائر لِلنَّاسِ﴾; had it been "hādhihi baṣāʾir li-l-nās" it would be correct. Similar is ﴿هَذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّى﴾; had it been "hādhihi raḥma", it would be permissible.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلاَ أَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى﴾: he says: were it not that Allah has made the punishment of this community deferred to the Day of Resurrection — that is the term — the punishment would have come to them. Then He said ﴿وَلَيَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ بَغْتَةً﴾, meaning the Resurrection; He made it masculine because He means the punishment of the Resurrection. And if you wish, you may make it masculine following the masculine of "term". Had it been ﴿وَلَتَأْتِيَنَّهُمْ﴾ it would be correct, meaning the Resurrection and the Hour.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَيِقُولُ ذُوقُواْ﴾: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (ويقال ذوقوا), and some read (وَنَقُولُ) with the nūn; all are correct.

farraa:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿يٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾: this is for the Muslims among the people of Mecca who were staying with the idolaters. He says ﴿إِنَّ أَرْضِي وَاسِعَةٌ﴾, meaning Medina, i.e. so do not live as neighbours of the people of disbelief.

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾: the generality read it ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾. Qays related to me from Abū Isḥāq that Ibn Masʿūd read it (لنُثْوِيَنَّهُمْ), and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it likewise. Both are good: bawwaʾtuhu manzilan and athwaytuhu manzilan (I lodged him in a dwelling).

farraa:60-60.t: His saying [Translator's note: the source has «وقولوا», a slip for «وقوله»]: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ﴾: it was revealed about the believers among the people of Mecca. When they were ordered to move away from it and go out to Medina, they said: O Messenger of Allah, we have no dwellings or wealth in Medina, so where will our livelihood come from? So Allah sent down ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن دَآبَّةٍ لاَّ تَحْمِلُ رِزْقَهَا﴾: it does not store its provision or gather it — i.e. so are all the creeping creatures of the earth, except the ant, for it stores its provision for its year.

farraa:64-64.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلآخِرَةَ لَهِيَ ٱلْحَيَوَانُ﴾: a life in which there is no death.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إِذَا هُمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: he says: they make their supplication and their affirmation of oneness sincerely for Allah at sea, and when He has saved them they turn to the worship of idols.

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُواْ﴾: ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it as a command and a rebuke, with the lām vowelless (wa-l-yatamattaʿū); and the people of the Hijaz read it ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعوا﴾ with kasra, in the sense of kay (in order that).
